questions.question: Write a design brief for feeding one hundred displaced people for a day, and list the specifications for energy, balance, quantities, adjustments and safety together with the constraints on the kitchen.
questions.expected_answer: Brief: plan and supply one day's food for one hundred people displaced by flooding and housed in a community hall, including babies, children, adults and the elderly, providing a nutritious balanced diet that can be stored without refrigeration and cooked on gas burners in large pots with limited water, so that no one goes hungry or becomes ill. Specifications: about 2 100 kilocalories per person, 210 000 for the camp, across three meals; a staple, protein, fat and vegetable or fruit every day; per person 400 grams of cereal, 60 grams of pulses or equivalent protein, 25 grams of oil, 15 grams of sugar, 5 grams of salt and 100 grams of vegetables, so 40 kilograms of staple, 6 kilograms of protein, 2.5 litres of oil, 1.5 kilograms of sugar, half a kilogram of salt and 10 kilograms of vegetables; soft enriched porridge for children under five and the elderly, rehydration salts available, no pork, rice for ten; all food cooked or opened within two hours of serving, water treated, hands washed. Constraints: R20 per person, R2 000; two gas burners and one fire, two pots at a time, no dish over an hour; 400 litres of water; dry storage without a fridge, nothing fresh beyond two days; breakfast by seven and lunch by one with four cooks; two 50 litre pots, one 20 litre pot, tin opener, knives and bowls.

questions.question: Plan a nutritious, tasty main meal for the camp, give the recipe for ten and scale it to one hundred, check it against the kitchen and state the three criteria by which it will be judged.
questions.expected_answer: Pap with a pilchard, tomato and onion relish and a side of cabbage gives staple, protein, fat and two vegetables, is familiar, contains no pork and uses two pots. For ten: 1.2 kilograms of maize meal and 4 litres of water for stiff pap; 2 tins of pilchards in tomato sauce, 1 tin of tomatoes, 2 onions, a tablespoon of oil, salt and a pinch of curry powder for the relish; half a cabbage, an onion and a tablespoon of oil for the side. For one hundred: 12 kilograms of meal, 40 litres of water, 20 tins of pilchards, 10 tins of tomatoes, 20 onions, 100 millilitres of oil, 5 cabbages. The 40 litres of pap fills a 50 litre pot and the relish and then the cabbage use the 20 litre pot; pap takes 30 minutes once boiling, relish 20 and cabbage 10, so the meal is ready in under an hour on two burners, using about 60 litres of water including washing up. A portion of pap is cooked thinner with milk powder and oil for children and the elderly. It is judged on nutrition, each plate carrying the four groups and about 700 kilocalories from 250 grams of pap, 150 of relish and 100 of cabbage; on flavour, onion, tomato, salt and spice making the fish appetising; and on texture, stiff pap for adults, soft for the young and old, relish with body and cabbage tender.

questions.question: Cost the planned day against the budget and describe the final checks and the contents of the one-page plan.
questions.expected_answer: The main meal costs about R120 for 12 kilograms of maize meal, R400 for 20 tins of pilchards, R150 for 10 tins of tomatoes, R60 for onions, R75 for cabbages and R30 for oil, salt and spice, about R835 or R8.35 a plate; a breakfast of soft porridge with sugar and milk powder adds about R3 a person and an evening meal of bread or rice with lentil soup about R6, so the day is about R17 to R18 a person, inside the R20 constraint with a margin for tea, fuel and rehydration salts; if over budget the fish is partly replaced by beans and tomato by cabbage. Final checks: soft enriched food for the young, old and sick, extra protein for pregnant and breastfeeding women, no pork, rice for ten; two pots at once, under an hour, four cooks, water in budget, nothing fresh kept beyond two days, tins opened just before cooking. The one page holds the brief, the two columns of specifications and constraints, the recipe for ten and the scaled list for one hundred, the cost table, the three evaluation criteria and the adjustments, and a team mate reads it as the cook arriving at six to find any gap.
